'''Michael Stewart Witherell''' (born 22 September 1949) is an American particle physicist<ref name=ACAPbio>[http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?witherellm Michael S. Witherell | Array of Contemporary Physicists]</ref>  and laboratory director emeritus of  [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], which he led from March, 2016 to June, 2026.<ref name=B/><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Director |url=https://www.lbl.gov/lab-leadership/director/ |access-date=2022-06-27 |website=Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory}}</ref><ref> {{Cite web |title= UC Names Katherine Yelick to Head Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory Berkeley Lab Director|url= https://newscenter.lbl.gov/2026/05/05/uc-names-katherine-yelick-to-head-lawrence-berkeley-national-laboratory/| website=Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|access-date=2026-05-05}}</ref> Witherell previously served as Director of [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory|Fermilab]], and was a professor and vice chancellor for research at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].

==Early life and education==
He was born 22 September 1949 in [[Toledo, Ohio]].<ref name=ACAPbio/> Witherell received a [[Bachelor of Science]] from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1968 and a [[Ph.D.]] from the  [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin, Madison]] in 1973.<ref name=ACAPbio/><ref name=":0" />

==Career==
From 1973 to 1981 he was on the faculty of [[Princeton University]].  He was a member of the physics faculty at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] from 1981 to 1999.<ref name=ACAPbio/>

In 1985 Witherell led an experiment at [[Fermilab]] which was the first to isolate a large sample of particles containing the [[charm quark]] using the new technology of silicon microstrip detectors.<ref name=A>{{cite web |url=https://www.fnal.gov/pub/ferminews/ferminews00-06-30/p2.html|title = Achievements of the Fixed Target Era (Ferminews, June 30, 2000)}}</ref>  He received the 1990 [[Panofsky Prize]] from the [[American Physical Society]] for this research. In 1998 he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].

Witherell served as the Director of the [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory|Fermilab]] from 1999 to 2005. In 2005 he returned to UC Santa Barbara as the Vice Chancellor for Research, serving in that role until 2016.<ref name=ACAPbio/>

In January 2016, the [[Regents of the University of California|University of California Board of Regents]] appointed him to be the Director of [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]].<ref name=B>{{cite web |url= http://newscenter.lbl.gov/2016/01/21/uc-names-michael-witherell-to-head-lawrence-berkeley-national-laboratory |title = UC names Michael Witherell to head Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory |date = 21 January 2016 |publisher= Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory}}</ref> In 2017 he was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref> {{cite web |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/michael-witherell|title=Dr. Michael Witherell |date=7 October 2023 | publisher = American Academy of Arts and Sciences}} </ref>

==Service to the national science enterprise==

Witherell is the chair of the National Academies' Committee on Science, Engineering, Medicine and Public Policy (COSEMPUP), starting in September, 2026.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.nationalacademies.org/units/PGA-COSEMPUP-21-P-435#organizers/| title = Committee on Science, Engineering, Medicine and Public Policy | website = National Academy of Sciences | access-date = September 9, 2026 }}</ref> He previously served on COSEMPUP from 2017-2021. He also served a three-year term on the National Academy of Sciences Council from 2023-2026.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.nasonline.org/about-the-nas/leadership/| title = Leadership and Governance: NAS Council | website = National Academy of Sciences | access-date = July 1, 2023 }}</ref>

Witherell chaired the Fermilab Program Advisory Committee from 1987 to 1989 and the [[SLAC]] Scientific Policy Committee from 1994 to 1996, and the [[High Energy Physics Advisory Panel]] of the [[United States Department of Energy]] from 1997 to 1999.<ref name=ACAPbio/> He chaired the Mathematical and Physical Sciences Advisory Committee (MPSAC) of the [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] from 2006 to 2008 and the National Academy of Science's Board on Physics and Astronomy from 2015 to 2016.

==Personal life==
His wife [[Elizabeth Witherell]], a literary historian and scholarly editor, is editor-in-chief of [[The Writings of Henry D. Thoreau]] project at UC Santa Barbara. <ref> {{cite web | url = 
https://thoreau.library.ucsb.edu/project_history.html | title = Project Direction and History | website = The Writings of Henry D. Thoreau | access-date = January 17, 2023}} </ref>

==Awards and honors==
*1986: elected a Fellow of the American Physical Society
*1988: Guggenheim Fellow for the academic year 1988–1989<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/michael-s-witherell/ John Simon Guggenheim Foundation | Michael S. Witherell]</ref>
*1990: awarded the [[Panofsky Prize]]
*1998: elected a member of the National Academy of Sciences
*2004: received the Gold Award of the US Secretary of Energy
*2017: elected a member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences
